Oceanus.definition: Ōceanus ī, m, *)wkeano/s, the great sea, outer sea, ocean: mare, quem Oceanum appellatis: Oceani freta, i. e. the Strait of Gibraltar: quae civitates Oceanum attingunt, Cs.: circumvagus, circumflu ent, H.: pater rerum…

October.definition: Octōber bris, bre, adj. octo, of the eighth month (later the tenth): Kalendae: a. d. III Nonas Octobrīs, September 29th.

Oedipus.definition: Oedipūs odis, m, *oi)di/pous, a king of Thebes, who solved the riddle of the Sphinx, C., O.—Prov.: Davus sum, non Oedipus, i. e. no diviner, T.

Olympia.definition: Olympia ōrum, n, *)olu/mpia, the Olympic games, games held every four years at Olympia, Enn. ap. C., H.

Olympias.definition: Olympias adis, f, *)olumpia/s, an Olympiad, interval of four years between Olympic games: prima.—Poet.: quinquennis, a period of five years (cf. lustrum), O.

Olympicus.definition: 'Olympicus adj., *)olumpiko/s, of the Olympic games: pulvis, H.'

Olympus.definition: Olympus (-pos) ī, m a high mountain on the borders of Macedonia and Thessaly, V., H.—The abode of the gods, heaven, sky: invito processit Vesper Olympo, V.: longus, the distant heavens, V.: (Iuppiter) totum nutu treme…

Orcus.definition: Orcus ī, m ARC-, the Lower World, prison of the dead, Orcus, V.— The god of the infernal regions, Orcus, Pluto, C., V., O.—The underworld, grave, death (poet.): ab Orco redux, T.: Orcum morari, hesitate to die, H.

Oreas.definition: Orēas adis, f, o)reia/s, a mountain-nymph, Oread, V.

Orgetorix.definition: Orgetorīx īgis, m a chief of the Helvetii, Cs.

Orion.definition: Ōrīōn or Orīōn ōnis or onis, m, *)wri/wn, a mythical giant, afterwards a constellation, C., V., H., O.

Ostiensis.definition: Ōstiēnsis e, adj., of Ostia, Ostian, C., L.: provincia, the superintendence of imports of corn: incommodum, the capture of a fleet by pirates at Ostia.

o.definition: ō (rarely, before a vowel o, V.), interj. of feeling or surprise, O! oh!: O vir fortis es, T.: o Romule, Romule die, Enn. ap. C.: o mi Furni!: o paterni generis oblite: O faciem pulchram, T.: o rem totam odiosam: o pi…

ob.definition: ob prep. with acc.—With verbs of motion, towards, to: cuius ob os Grai ora obvertebant sua, Poët. ap. C.: Turni se pestis ob ora Fert, V.— With verbs of rest, before, in front of, over against: non mihi mors ob oculos…

obaeratus.definition: obaerātus adj. with comp. ob+aes, involved in debt: plebs, L.: quanto quis obaeratior, Ta.— Plur m. as subst, debtors: obaeratos liberare.

obambulo.definition: ob-ambulō āvī, —, āre, to walk before, go around: muris, L.: (lupus) gregibus obambulat, prowls about, V.: Aetnam, O.—To walk about, wander: ante vallum, L.: solus, O.

obarmo.definition: ob-armō —, —, āre, to arm: securi Dextras, H.

obaro.definition: ob-arō āvī, —, āre, to plough around, plough up: quicquid herbidi terreni erat, L.

obdo.definition: ob-dō didī, ditus, ere, to put against, shut, close, fasten: pessulum ostio, slip the bolt, T.: nulli malo latus apertum, expose, H.

obdormisco.definition: obdormīscō īvī, —, ere, inch. * ob-dormio, to fall asleep: in mediis vitae laboribus.

obduco.definition: ob-dūcō dūxī, ductus, ere, to draw before, draw forward, bring over: Curium, to bring forward (as a candidate): ab utroque latere collis fossam, extend, Cs.—To close over, cover over, overspread, surround, envelop: tr…

obductio.definition: ob-ductiō ōnis, f obduco, a covering, enveloping: capitis (before execution).

obductus.definition: obductus adj. P. of obduco, overspread, clouded, gloomy: obductā nocte, O.: fronte, H., Iu.

obduresco.definition: ob-dūrēscō ruī, —, ere, to grow hard: Gorgonis voltu, i. e. to be petrified, Pr.—To become hardened, grow insensible, be obdurate: usu obduruerat civitatis patientia: animus ad dolorem: quorum (amicorum) alii obduruer…

obduro.definition: ob-dūrō āvī, ātus, āre, to be hard, hold out, persist, endure: persta atque obdura, H.: perfer et obdura, O.—Pass impers.: quā re obduretur hoc triduum, ut, etc.

obeliscus.definition: obeliscus ī, m, o)beli/skos, an obelisk, Ta.

obeo.definition: ob-eō īvī, itus, īre, to go, go to meet, go in opposition: infera in loca: ad omnīs hostium conatūs, L.—Of heavenly bodies, to go down, set: obit Lepus.—To fall, perish, die: tecum libens, H.: simul se cum illis obitu…

obequito.definition: ob-equitō āvī, —, āre, to ride towards, ride up to: obequitando castris, L.: portis, L.

oberro.definition: ob-errō —, —, āre, to wander among, ramble about: tentoriis, Ta.: cum periculi imago oculis oberraret, hovered before, Cu.—To err, mistake: chordā semper eādem, blunder at, H.

obesus.definition: ōbēsus adj. P. of * ob-edo, that has eaten, fat, stout, plump: turdus, H.: fauces, swollen, V. —Fig., gross, indelicate, dull: invenis naris obesae, H.

obex.definition: (ōbex, ōbicis) m and f ob+IA-, a bolt, bar, barrier, wall (only abl sing. and nom, acc. and abl plur.): obices portarum, L.: fultos emuniit obice postes, V.: obice firmo Clauserat, O.: maria tumescant Obicibus ruptis,…

obgannio.definition: ob-ganniō —, —, īre, to snarl at: ei alqd ad aurem, T.

obiacens.definition: ob-iacēns ntis, P. P. praes. of ob-iaceo, lying before, lying near, in the way: sarcinarum cumulus, L.: saxa pedibus, L.

obicio.definition: obiciō (not obiiciō), iēcī, iectus, ere ob+ iacio, to throw before, throw to, cast, offer, present, expose: corpus feris: alcui offam, V.: legatum hominibus feris, Cs.: si tale visum obiectum est a deo dormienti, pres…

obiectatio.definition: obiectātiō ōnis, f obiecto, a reproach, Cs.

obiecto.definition: obiectō āvī, ātus, āre, freq. obicio, to set against, oppose: caput fretis, i. e. dive, V.—Fig., to abandon, expose, endanger: se hostium telis, L.: eum periculis, S.: caput periclis, V.: pro cunctis unam animam, V.—T…

obiectus1.definition: obiectus adj. P. of obicio, lying before, opposite: nec visi obiectis silvis, because of the woods in front, Cs.: insula Alexandriae, Cs.: flumina, V.: obiectus fortunae, exposed: ad omnes casūs periculorum.—Plur n. a…

obiectus2.definition: (obiectus, ūs) m ob+IA-, a putting against, opposing: miles tectus plutei obiectu, Cs.: insula portum Efficit obiectu laterum, opposition, V.: molium obiectūs scandere (i. e. moles obiectas), Ta.

obiratus.definition: ob-īrātus adj., angered, angry: fortunae, L.

obiter.definition: ob-iter adv., on the way, while travelling: leget aut scribet, Iu.— Meanwhile, incidentally: Verberat atque obiter faciem linit (i. e. inter verberandum), Iu.

obitus.definition: obitus (ūs), m ob+1 I-, an approach, visit, T.—A going down, setting: siderum: signorum, V.—Downfall, ruin, destruction, death: regis: post eorum obitum, Cs.: Difficiles obitūs, painful death, V.: post obitum vestrum,…

obiurgatio.definition: obiūrgātiō ōnis, f obiurgo, a chiding, reproof, rebuke, scolding, remonstrance: ut obiurgatio contumeliā careat: lenior.

obiurgator.definition: obiūrgātor ōris, m obiurgo, a chider, scold noster.— Plur: benevoli.

obiurgatorius.definition: obiūrgātōrius adj. obiurgator, chiding, scolding: epistula.

obiurgo.definition: ob-iūrgō āvī, ātus, āre, to chide, scold, blame, rebuke, reprove: ad obiurgandum causa, T.: Caelium: me de Pompei familiaritate, moderately: cum obiurgarer, quod nimio gaudio paene desiperem.—To urge, adjure, exhort e…

oblanguesco.definition: ob-languēscō guī, —, ere, inch, to become feeble, languish: litterulae meae oblanguerunt.

oblectamen.definition: (oblectāmen, inis) n oblecto, a delight.— Only plur: hominum, sources of consolation, O.

oblectamentum.definition: oblectāmentum ī, n oblecto, a delight, pleasure, amusement: senectutis: oblectamenta et solacia servitutis: rerum rusticarum.

oblectatio.definition: ob-lectātiō ōnis, f oblecto, a delighting, delight: requies plena oblectationis fuit: vitae.

oblecto.definition: ob-lectō āvī, ātus, āre 2 lacto, to delight, divert, entertain, amuse, interest: se: populum, H.: animum, Iu.: senectutem: se agri cultione: me te (abl.), T.: ludis oblectamur: te cum Cicerone: In eo me oblecto, he is…

oblido.definition: oblīdō —, —, ere ob + laedo, to squeeze together, compress: caelum digitulis: oblisis faucibus, strangled, Ta.

obligatio.definition: obligātiō ōnis, f obligo, an engaging, pledging, obligation: est gravior animi quam pecuniae.

obligo.definition: ob-ligō āvī, ātus, āre, to bind up, bandage, swathe: volnus: bracchia, T.—Fig., to bind, oblige, put under obligation, make liable: eum militiae sacramento, swear in again: vadem tribus milibus aeris, bind in the sum …

oblimo.definition: oblīmō āvī, ātus, āre ob+limus, to cover with mud, deluge, besmear: oblimati agri: sulcos, V. —To scatter, lavish, squander, dissipate: rem patris, H.

oblino.definition: ob-linō lēvī, litus, ere, to daub, smear over, bedaub, besmear: unguentis obliti: sanguine, O.: oblitus faciem cruore, Ta.—Fig., to smear, befoul, defile: se externis moribus: omnia dedecore oblita: alquem versibus at…

oblique.definition: oblīquē adv. obliquus, athwart, obliquely: ferri.—Indirectly, covertly: alqm castigare, Ta.

obliquo.definition: oblīquō āvī, ātus, āre obliquus, to turn aside, twist, turn awry: oculos, O.: crinem, draw back, Ta.: sinūs (velorum) in ventum, slant, V.

obliquus.definition: oblīquus or oblīcus adj. 2 LAC-, sidelong, slanting, awry, oblique, crosswise: motus corporis: obliquo claudicare pede, O.: iter, Cs.: chordae, i. e. of the triangular harp, Iu.: ictus, H.: obliquo dente timendus aper…

oblitesco.definition: oblitēscō —, —, ere, inch. ob+latesco, to hide, conceal oneself: a nostro aspectu.

oblittero.definition: oblitterō (oblīt-) āvī, ātus, āre see LI-, to blot out, erase: litterae oblitteratae, Ta.—Fig., to blot out of remembrance, cause to be forgotten: benefici memoriā offensionem: adversam prosperā pugnā, L.: res vetusta…

oblitus2.definition: oblītus adj. P. of obliviscor, forgetful, unmindful, not remembering: sui: veterum honorum, O.—Forgetful, regardless, indifferent, neglectful: Illum gementem Obliti relinquunt, V.: pectus, Ct.: mei, i. e. of my dignit…

oblivio.definition: oblīviō ōnis, f LIV-, a being forgotten, forgetfulness, oblivion: veteris belli: hominum: (sacra) oblivioni dare, consign to oblivion, L.: iniurias oblivione contriveram, buried: in oblivionem negoti venire, forget: n…

obliviosus.definition: oblīviōsus adj. oblivio, that easily forgets, forgetful, oblivious: senes.—Producing forgetfulness, oblivious: Massicus, H.

obliviscor.definition: oblīvīscor lītus, ī ob+LIV-, to forget: cui placet obliviscitur: Latine, forget their mother tongue: oblitus sum mei, have forgotten myself, T.: sceleris eorum, S.: veteris contumeliae, Cs.: artificium: concilia, L.: …

oblivium.definition: oblīvium ī, n obliviscor, forgetfulness, oblivion: sententiam oblivio transmittere, T.—Usu. plur: longa oblivia potant, V.: Ducere oblivia vitae, H.: Herculeae oblivia laudis Acta tibi, that you have forgotten, O.

oblongus.definition: 'ob-longus adj., more long than wide, oblong: aedificia, S.: scutula, Ta.'

obloquor.definition: ob-loquor locūtus, ī, dep., to speak against, interrupt, contradict, rail at, abuse: ut me et interpelles, et obloquare: mihi: gannit et obloquitur, Ct.—To sing to, accompany, join in singing: non avis obloquitur, O.:…

obluctor.definition: ob-luctor ātus, ārī, dep., to struggle against, contend with, oppose: genibus adversae harenae, V.—Fig.: animus obluctans difficultatibus, Cu.

obmolior.definition: ob-mōlior ītus, īrī, dep., to push before, throw up before (as a defence or obstruction): nec in promptu erat quod obmolirentur, L.: arborum truncos et saxa, Cu.—To block up, obstruct, L.

obmurmuro.definition: ob-murmurō āvī, ātus, āre, to murmur against: precibus meis, O.

obmutesco.definition: ob-mūtēscō tuī, —, ere, inch. mutus, to become dumb, lose one's speech, be silent: homo loquacissimus obmutuit: aspectu, V.: dolore, O. —Fig., to become silent, cease: studium nostrum obmutuit: animi dolor.

obnatus.definition: ob-nātus adj., growing on, growing over: obnata ripis salicta, L.

obnitor.definition: ob-nītor nīxus, ī, dep., to bear upon, press against, struggle with, strain at: remi Obnixi crepuere, V.: obnixi urgebant, L.: obnixo genu scuto, pressed against, N.: Arboris trunco, V.: manu hostibus, Ta.—Fig., to st…

obnixe.definition: obnīxē adv., with all one's strength, strenuously, obstinately: omnia Facturus, T.

obnixus.definition: obnīxus (not obnīsus), adj. P. of obnitor, strenuous, firm, resolute: (velim) obnixos vos impetum hostium excipere, L.: curam sub corde premebat, V.: non cedere, V.

obnoxie.definition: obnoxiē adv. obnoxius, slavishly, timidly: sententias dicere, L.

obnoxius.definition: ob-noxius adj., liable, addicted, guilty: animus lubidini, S.: Terra nulli obnoxia bello, exposed, O.: Obnoxium est (with infin.), it is dangerous, Ta. — Subject, submissive, obedient, complying, servile: vobis, L.: p…

obnubilus.definition: ob-nūbilus adj., clouded over: tenebris loca, Enn. ap. C.

obnubo.definition: ob-nūbō nūpsī, nūptus, ere, to veil, cover: caput, C., L. (old law forms): comas amictu, V.

obnuntiatio.definition: obnūntiātiō (not obnūnc-), ōnis, f obnuntio, of an augur, an announcement of an adverse omen, evil interpretation: dirarum.— Plur., C.

obnuntio.definition: ob-nūntiō āvī, ātus, āre, to tell, report, announce (of bad news): Primus obnuntio, T.—In augury, to announce an adverse omen, prevent by declaring unfavorable auspices: consul consuli obnuntiasti.

oboediens.definition: oboediēns (not obēd-), entis, adj. with comp. and sup. P. of oboedio, obedient, subject, compliant: Omnia oboedientia sunt, reduced to subjection, S.: cuius vis omnis in consensu oboedientium esset, the obedient, L.: …

oboedienter.definition: 'oboedienter adv. with comp. oboediens, obediently, willingly, submissively: imperata facturi, L.: adversus Romanos faciebat, L.: nihil oboedientius fecerunt, quam, etc., L.'

oboedientia.definition: 'oboedientia ae, f oboediens, obedience: abiciunt oboedientiam: fracti animi.'

oboedio.definition: oboediō not obēdiō, īvī, ītus, īre ob+audio, to give ear, hearken, listen: alquibus, N.—To obey, yield obedience, be subject, serve: ad verba nobis: praecepto: legi, N.: libidines voluptatibus: pecora ventri, S.—Pass …

obolus.definition: obolus ī, m, o)bolo/s, a small Greek coin, a sixth of a drachma (about three cents, or three halfpence): Holera ferre obolo, T.

oborior.definition: ob-orior ortus, īrī, dep., to arise, appear, spring up: lacrimae omnibus obortae, L.: saxo concrevit oborto, i. e. was turned to stone, O.: laetitia obortast, T.: quanta lux liberalitatis mihi oboriatur.

obrepo.definition: ob-rēpō rēpsī, rēptus, ere, to creep up, approach stealthily, steal upon, come suddenly upon, surprise: obrepsit dies: obrepit non intellecta senectus, Iu.: operi longo fas est obrepere somnum, H.: ad honorem, reach s…

obrigesco.definition: ob-rigēscō riguī, —, ere, inch, to stiffen, become stiff: paene: pars (terrae) obriguerit pruinā.

obrogo.definition: ob-rogō āvī, ātus, āre, in legislation, to repeal by implication, supersede, invalidate by a new law: huic legi nec obrogari fas est, etc.: antiquae (legi) obrogat nova, L.

obruo.definition: ob-ruō uī, utus, ere, to overwhelm, overthrow, cover, cover over, hide, bury: ibi vivi obruerentur, be buried alive, S.: confossus undique obruitur, Cu.: sese harenā, hide in the sand: thesaurum, bury.—To sink, submer…

obrussa.definition: 'obrussa ae, f, o)/bruzon, a test, touchstone, proof: tamquam obrussa ratio.'

obsaepio.definition: ob-saepiō (-sēpiō), psī, ptus, ere, to hedge in, fence in, close, render impassable: itinera, L.— Fig., to close, bar up: viam adipiscendi: ut obsaeptum plebi sit ad honorem iter, L.

obsaturo.definition: ob-saturō —, —, āre, to sate, cloy: istius obsaturari, have enough of him, T.

obscene.definition: obscēnē (obscaenē) adv. with comp. obscenus, immodestly, indecently, obscenely: dici: obscenius excitata.

obscenitas.definition: obscēnitās (obscaen-) ātis, f obscenus, moral impurity, foulness, unchastity, lewdness, obscenity: turpissima: si quod sit in obscenitate flagitium.

obscenus.definition: obscēnus (obscaen-, not obscoenus), adj. with comp. and sup. 1 SAV-, of adverse omen, ill-omened, ill-boding, inauspicious, ominous, portentous: volucres, of ill-omen, V.: animalium fetūs, monstrous, L.: omen: puppis,…

obscuratio.definition: obscūrātiō ōnis, f obscuro, a darkening, obscuring: solis.—Fig.: in voluptatibus, i. e. disregard.—Plur., C.

obscure.definition: obscūrē adv. with comp. and sup. obscurus, darkly, obscurely: cernere, dimly.—Fig., covertly, closely, secretly: agere: alqd ferre: obscurius iniqui, more secretly: quam obscurissime.

obscuritas.definition: obscūritās ātis, f obscurus, darkness, obscurity, indistinctness, uncertainty: latebrarum, Ta.: in obscuritate latere: naturae: obscuritates somniorum. —Of rank, insignificance, obscurity, meanness: humilitas et obscu…

obscuro.definition: obscūrō āvī, ātus, āre obscurus, to render dark, darken, obscure: obscuratur luce solis lumen lucernae: caelum nocte obscuratum, S.: volucres Aethera obscurant pennis, V.: obscuratus sol, eclipsed.—To hide, conceal, c…

obscurus.definition: obscūrus adj. with comp. and sup. 1 SCV-, dark, darksome, dusky, shady, obscure: umbra, C. poët.: lucus, V.: antrum, O.: tabernae, H.: lux, L.: lumen, darkness visible, S.: caelum, H.: ferrugo, black, V.: dentes, blac…

obsecratio.definition: obsecrātiō ōnis, f obsecro, a beseeching, imploring, supplication, entreaty: eius.—As a rhetorical figure, C.—A public prayer: a populo facta, L.—Plur., C.

obsecro.definition: obsecrō āvī, ātus, āre ob+sacro, to beseech, entreat, implore, supplicate, conjure: cum multis lacrimis: pro fratris salute: te per senectutem suam, conjures you: pro salute meā populum R.: hoc te obsecro, T.: illud u…

obsecundo.definition: ob-secundō āvī, ātus, āre, to comply, humor, yield, be accommodating: in loco, seasonably, T.: obsecundando mollire impetum, L.: alcui: eius voluntatibus.

obsequens.definition: obsequēns entis, adj. with comp. P. of obsequor, yielding, compliant, obsequious, accommodating: patri, T.: legiones nobis: Persae obsequentiores, Cu.

obsequenter.definition: obsequenter adv. obsequens, compliantly, obsequiously: haec a collegā facta, L.

obsequentia.definition: 'obsequentia ae, f obsequens, complaisance, obsequiousness: reliquorum, Cs.'

obsequium.definition: obsequium ī, n SEC-, compliance, yieldingness, complaisance, indulgence: Obsequium amicos parit, T.: Antonium obsequio mitigavi: ventris, i. e. gluttony, H.: peritura amantis Obsequio, to her lover, O.: Flectitur obse…

obsequor.definition: ob-sequor cūtus (not quūtus), ī, dep., to comply, yield, gratify, humor, submit, be accommodating: tibi, T.: huic: voluntati tuae: imperio, Iu.: uti de Pompilio referrent, senatui, L.—To yield, give up, indulge: animo…

obsero1.definition: obserō āvī, ātus, āre 1 SER-, to bolt, bar, fasten, shut up: ostium intus, T.: aedificia, L.: aurīs, H.

obsero2.definition: ob-serō sēvī, situs, ere, to sow, plant: terram frugibus.— P. perf., covered over, covered, strewn, filled: obsiti virgultis colles, L.: pomis Rura, O.: aeger pannis annisque, T.: montes nivibus, Cu.: Io iam setis obs…

observans.definition: observāns antis, adj. with sup. P. of observo, watchful, attentive, respectful: homo tui: observantissimus mei.

observantia.definition: observantia ae, f observo, attention, respect, regard, reverence: observantiam dilexit: amicos observantiā retinere: in regem, L.

observatio.definition: observātiō ōnis, f observo, a watching, observance, investigation: observationes animadvertebant, your searches for evidence: siderum.— Circumspection, care, exactness: summa in bello movendo.

observito.definition: observitō āvī, —, āre, freq. observo, to watch carefully, observe closely: motūs stellarum.

observo.definition: ob-servō āvī, ātus, āre, to watch, note, heed, observe, take notice of, attend to: filium, Quid agat, T.: fetūs, watch for, V.: occupationem eius: tempus epistulae tibi reddendae, watch for: sese, keep a close watch o…

obses.definition: obses idis (gen plur. obsidum, rarely obsidium, Cs., L.), m and f SED-, a hostage: obsides uti inter sese dent, exchange, Cs.: Cretensibus obsides imperavit: multi Romanis dediti obsides, S.: alqm obsidem retinere, as…

obsessio.definition: obsessiō ōnis, f obsideo, a blocking up, be sieging, blockade: militaris viae: nostrorum, Cs.

obsessor.definition: obsessor ōris, m a frequenter, haunter, resident: aquarum (of a water-snake), O.—A besieger<*> invester, blockader: curiae: Luceriae, L.

obsideo.definition: obsideō ēdī, essus, ēre ob+sedeo, to sit, stay, remain, abide: domi, T.—To beset, haunt, frequent: umbilicum terrarum.—In war, to hem in, beset, besiege, invest, blockade: quod (oppidum) neque capi neque obsideri pote…

obsidialis.definition: obsidiālis e, adj. obsidium, of a siege: graminea corona, for raising a siege, L.

obsidio.definition: obsidiō ōnis, f ob, a siege, investment, blockade: urbis, Cs.: obsidione urbīs capere: Bibulum in obsidione habere, Cs.: spes maior in obsidione quam in oppugnatione, L.: obsidione Isiondensīs exemit, released from, L…

obsidium1.definition: obsidium ī, n ob+SED-, a siege, blockade: obsidio circumdare, Ta.

obsidium2.definition: obsidium ī, n obses, the condition of a hostage, hostageship: obsidio nobis datus, Ta.

obsido.definition: ob-sīdō —, —, ere, to beset, invest, besiege, blockade: pontem, S.: excubiis portas, V.: Italos finīs, take possession of, V.: campos, i. e. to buy, Tb.
